questions.q: A 35-year-old male presents with a painless genital ulcer with indurated edges and clean base, followed by bilateral inguinal lymphadenopathy. Dark-field microscopy shows corkscrew motility organisms. What is the most appropriate treatment?
opts: Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU IM single dose
questions.exp: Primary syphilis caused by Treponema pallidum. Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU IM single dose is the treatment of choice for primary/secondary syphilis.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman develops a butterfly rash on face, oral ulcers, and joint pain. ANA is positive (1:640), anti-dsDNA elevated. Skin biopsy shows thickening of basement membrane with IgG and C3 deposits on direct immunofluorescence. Which pattern is characteristic?
questions.exp: SLE shows granular (lupus band) deposits of IgG, IgM, C3 at the DEJ on DIF. Linear pattern is seen in bullous pemphigoid, intercellular in pemphigus.

questions.q: A 55-year-old farmer presents with verrucous plaques on the leg with black dots visible on the surface. Biopsy shows Medlar bodies (copper penny sclerotic cells). Which organism is most likely responsible?
questions.exp: Chromoblastomycosis presents with verrucous plaques. Medlar (sclerotic/copper-penny) bodies are pathognomonic. F. pedrosoi is the most common causative organism.

questions.q: A 40-year-old man on long-term dapsone therapy for leprosy develops sudden-onset pallor and fatigue. CBC shows Hb 7g/dL with heinz bodies and bite cells on peripheral smear. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Dapsone causes hemolysis particularly in G6PD-deficient patients. Heinz bodies and bite cells are characteristic of oxidative hemolysis due to dapsone.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman presents with tense bullae on erythematous skin. Biopsy shows subepidermal bulla with eosinophils. DIF shows linear IgG and C3 along the BMZ. ELISA is positive for BP180 antibody. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid: tense subepidermal bullae, linear IgG/C3 at BMZ, anti-BP180 (BPAG2) antibodies. BP180 is the main target antigen in BP.

questions.q: A 50-year-old man presents with scaly erythematous plaques on elbows, knees, and scalp. Auspitz sign is positive. Histopathology shows Munro microabscesses and parakeratosis. Which cytokine is the primary driver of this condition?
questions.exp: Psoriasis is primarily driven by the IL-23/IL-17 axis. IL-17A produced by Th17 cells is the key pathogenic cytokine. Biologics targeting IL-17A (secukinumab, ixekizumab) are highly effective.

questions.q: A 30-year-old HIV-positive patient (CD4: 80) presents with multiple painless umbilicated papules on face, neck, and genitals. The lesions express viral inclusions on Wright stain. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Molluscum contagiosum caused by poxvirus. In immunocompromised patients (HIV), lesions are numerous and giant. Umbilicated papules with intracytoplasmic Henderson-Paterson bodies on histology.

questions.q: A leprosy patient shows thickened great auricular nerve, ulnar nerve at elbow, and common peroneal nerve. Skin smear shows AFB with BI of 4+. No reversal reaction. What type of leprosy does this patient have?
questions.exp: High BI (4+), multiple nerve involvement, and lepromatous features indicate LL leprosy. LL is multibacillary with high bacterial load and symmetric nerve involvement.

questions.q: A 45-year-old diabetic develops painful, rapidly spreading cellulitis on the lower leg with crepitus on palpation and gas on X-ray. Blood culture shows gram-positive rods. What is the most appropriate immediate management?
questions.exp: Gas gangrene (necrotizing fasciitis) requires urgent surgical debridement. Combined with broad-spectrum antibiotics (penicillin + clindamycin). Delay increases mortality.

questions.q: A 20-year-old develops extensive flaccid bullae, erosions in mouth, and Nikolsky sign positive. Biopsy shows suprabasal acantholysis with tombstone pattern. DIF shows intercellular IgG (fish-net/chicken-wire pattern). Which antigen is targeted?
questions.exp: Pemphigus vulgaris targets Desmoglein 3 (mucosal dominant) and sometimes Dsg1. Suprabasal acantholysis with intercellular IgG on DIF is characteristic.

questions.q: A 60-year-old man presents with a pearly, translucent nodule with telangiectasias on his nose. Biopsy shows nests of basaloid cells with peripheral palisading. What is the most common site for this tumor?
questions.exp: Basal cell carcinoma most commonly occurs on sun-exposed areas, particularly the nose (most common site) and periorbital region. Peripheral palisading of basaloid cells is characteristic.

questions.q: A 32-year-old woman on methotrexate for psoriasis develops stomatitis, macrocytic anemia, and elevated LFTs. What supplementation should be given to reduce toxicity?
questions.exp: Methotrexate is a folate antagonist. Folic acid supplementation (5mg daily, given on non-methotrexate days) reduces mucosal and GI toxicity without compromising efficacy.

questions.q: A 25-year-old with new-onset atopic dermatitis fails topical corticosteroids and topical calcineurin inhibitors. Which biologic agent is currently approved as first-line biologic for moderate-severe AD?
questions.exp: Dupilumab (anti-IL-4Rα) blocks IL-4 and IL-13 signaling and is FDA/DCGI approved for moderate-severe atopic dermatitis. It is the first biologic approved for AD.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman develops purpuric papules on lower extremities, arthralgias, and hematuria. Serum complement C3 and C4 are low. Biopsy shows leukocytoclastic vasculitis. Hepatitis C serology is positive. What is the most likely mechanism?
questions.exp: HCV-associated mixed cryoglobulinemia type II presents with palpable purpura, arthralgias, and renal involvement. Cryoglobulins (IgM-IgG immune complexes) deposit in vessels causing vasculitis with low complement.

questions.q: A woodworker presents with a painless nodule on the dorsum of hand that developed sporotrichoid spread up the forearm. KOH mount is negative. Biopsy shows cigar-shaped yeast at 37°C. What is the treatment of choice?
questions.exp: Sporotrichosis (Sporothrix schenckii) classically shows sporotrichoid (lymphocutaneous) spread. Cigar-shaped yeast at 37°C. Itraconazole 200mg/day for 3-6 months is the treatment of choice.

questions.q: A 35-year-old woman presents with Raynaud's phenomenon, puffy fingers, and dysphagia. ANA shows nucleolar pattern. Anti-Scl-70 (anti-topoisomerase I) antibody is positive. What is the most feared complication?
questions.exp: Anti-topoisomerase I (Scl-70) is associated with diffuse cutaneous SSc. Scleroderma renal crisis (hypertensive urgency with microangiopathic hemolysis) is the most feared acute complication of diffuse SSc.

questions.q: A leprosy patient on MDT develops sudden painful erythema nodosum leprosum (ENL). Which treatment is most effective for severe ENL?
questions.exp: Thalidomide is the most effective drug for severe/recurrent ENL due to its anti-TNF-alpha action. It is contraindicated in women of childbearing age due to teratogenicity. Prednisolone is used when thalidomide is contraindicated.

questions.q: A 22-year-old presents with clustered vesicles on an erythematous base along a dermatome on the chest. The patient reports burning pain that preceded the rash by 3 days. What is the first-line antiviral treatment for a healthy adult?
opts: Oral acyclovir 800mg 5 times daily for 7 days
questions.exp: Herpes zoster treatment: valacyclovir 1g TID for 7 days is preferred in immunocompetent adults due to better bioavailability compared to acyclovir. Famciclovir 500mg TID is an alternative. IV acyclovir is for immunocompromised/severe cases.

questions.q: A patient presents with hypopigmented anesthetic macules on the trunk with a few satellite lesions. Slit-skin smear is negative. Lepromin test shows 15mm induration at 28 days. How should this patient be classified?
questions.exp: WHO classification: PB leprosy = 1-5 patches, negative SSS. MB = 6+ patches or positive SSS. This patient has few patches with negative SSS → PB → 6 months MDT (rifampicin + dapsone).

questions.q: During a Mohs micrographic surgery, the surgeon excises tissue in stages. What is the main advantage of Mohs surgery over wide local excision for BCC?
opts: Highest cure rate with maximum tissue conservation
questions.exp: Mohs surgery provides real-time microscopic examination of 100% of the margins (horizontal frozen sections), resulting in the highest cure rates (99% for primary BCC) while maximizing tissue conservation. Ideal for facial BCCs.

questions.q: A 55-year-old woman presents with violaceous flat-topped papules on wrists and buccal mucosa with white reticulate lines (Wickham striae). Histopathology shows saw-tooth rete ridges, hypergranulosis, and band-like lymphocytic infiltrate. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Lichen planus: 4 Ps (Pruritic, Purple, Polygonal, Planar papules). Wickham striae on buccal mucosa. Histology: saw-tooth rete ridges, hypergranulosis, vacuolar degeneration of basal layer, band-like lymphocytic infiltrate.

questions.q: A 28-year-old man presents with condylomata acuminata (anogenital warts). HPV typing shows HPV 6 and 11. Which HPV types are associated with the highest risk of anogenital carcinoma?
questions.exp: HPV 16 and 18 are high-risk oncogenic types responsible for >70% of cervical and anogenital cancers. HPV 6 and 11 cause condylomata acuminata (low-risk, benign warts).

questions.q: A 40-year-old man develops extensive superficial desquamation involving >90% BSA after stopping systemic steroids. The scale is fine and diffuse without systemic symptoms. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Erythroderma (>90% BSA involvement with erythema and scaling) can be triggered by abrupt steroid withdrawal. The patient needs hospitalization, fluid/electrolyte management, and controlled re-introduction of systemic therapy.

questions.q: A 30-year-old woman on oral contraceptives develops brownish hyperpigmentation on cheeks, upper lip, and forehead in a symmetric distribution. The pigmentation worsens with sun exposure. Wood's lamp shows enhancement of pigmentation. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Melasma: symmetric hyperpigmentation on sun-exposed face, triggered/worsened by OCP, pregnancy, UV. Wood's lamp enhancement indicates epidermal melanin (responds better to treatment than dermal type).

questions.q: A 45-year-old man presents with a rapidly growing, well-circumscribed crater-form nodule with a central keratin plug on the cheek that appeared over 6 weeks. Histology shows well-differentiated squamous epithelium with a central keratin-filled crater. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Keratoacanthoma: rapidly growing crateriform nodule with central keratin plug. Resembles well-differentiated SCC histologically. Spontaneously regresses in 3-6 months. Treated as low-grade SCC (excision recommended to exclude SCC).

questions.q: A 65-year-old woman develops grouped pruritic vesicles on elbows, knees, and buttocks. Biopsy shows subepidermal vesicle with neutrophils at dermal papilla tips. DIF shows granular IgA at tips of dermal papillae. Endomysial antibodies are positive. What is the first-line treatment?
questions.exp: Dermatitis herpetiformis (Duhring's disease): gluten-sensitive enteropathy, granular IgA at dermal papilla tips, associated with HLA-DQ2/DQ8. Treatment: dapsone (rapid relief) + strict lifelong gluten-free diet (treats underlying cause).

questions.q: A neonate develops blistering at sites of minor trauma, with milia formation and scarring. Electron microscopy shows cleavage within the lamina lucida. Inheritance is autosomal recessive. Which protein is defective?
questions.exp: Junctional EB (Herlitz type) shows cleavage in lamina lucida. The defective protein is laminin 332 (or integrin alpha-6-beta-4 or BPAG2). Keratin 5/14 → EB simplex (intraepidermal). Type VII collagen → dystrophic EB (sub-lamina densa).

questions.q: A 55-year-old with PUVA therapy for psoriasis for 10 years presents with a rapidly growing ulcerated nodule on the forearm. Histology shows atypical keratinocytes with individual cell keratinization and keratin pearls invading the dermis. What is the most significant risk factor in this patient?
questions.exp: Long-term PUVA therapy significantly increases the risk of squamous cell carcinoma (and to a lesser extent BCC). The cumulative PUVA dose is directly proportional to SCC risk; patients require regular skin surveillance.

questions.q: A 20-year-old man presents with recurrent oral ulcers, genital ulcers, uveitis, and pathergy test positive. HLA-B51 is positive. What is the most effective treatment for severe ocular disease in this condition?
questions.exp: Behcet's disease (oral + genital ulcers + uveitis, HLA-B51). Anti-TNF agents (infliximab, adalimumab) are most effective for severe ocular disease and refractory cases. Colchicine helps mucocutaneous disease.

questions.q: A 38-year-old woman presents with photosensitivity, discoid plaques with follicular plugging and atrophic scarring on the scalp, and malar erythema. ANA is weakly positive. Anti-Ro/SSA is positive. What type of lupus is this most consistent with?
questions.exp: Discoid LE: chronic scarring plaques with follicular plugging, telangiectasia, dyspigmentation, and atrophic scarring—especially on scalp causing scarring alopecia. Confined to skin (10-15% progress to SLE). Anti-dsDNA typically negative.

questions.q: A 52-year-old HIV-positive man (CD4: 50) presents with indurated, non-healing perianal ulcers for 3 months. Dark-field microscopy and serology confirm syphilis. Standard benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU was given. How should follow-up serology be interpreted?
opts: RPR decline by 2 dilutions at 6 months = treatment success
Any reactive RPR at 3 months = treatment failure
VDRL must become non-reactive at 1 month
questions.exp: Treatment success in syphilis: 4-fold (2 dilution) decline in non-treponemal titer (RPR/VDRL) at 6 months (12 months for late syphilis). FTA-ABS remains reactive for life and cannot be used to assess cure.
